notes.text: A battery divider into a buffer: the divider's node feeds the amplifier's input, the amplifier's output is wired back to its inverting input, and a resistor and a capacitor filter the output before it leaves for the converter.

A buck converter: the input and output capacitors, the inductor from the switching node to the output, the bootstrap capacitor between the BST and SW pins, the divider that sets the output from the feedback pin, a resistor on RT and a pull-up on the power-good flag.
A regulator with a capacitor on its input and one on its output.
The microcontroller, an 8 MHz crystal on its oscillator pins, and two supply capacitors.

A radio modem's side of the board: a four-pin serial connector and a four-pin control connector, pull-ups and pull-downs on the lines, a status light, an RC on each of five lines and three capacitors on the supply. Twenty-two parts, one drawing (the old drawing cut a module of more than twenty in two).
A connector with ground pins, pins left open and three signals.
A connector whose ten pins all go on to another module.
